# Abstract {#abstract}

This synthetic research note is a visual fixture rather than a scientific claim. It tests a conventional hierarchy, a readable prose measure and restrained evidence presentation under the same theme used by the other gallery documents. No obligatory metric row, feature card or decorative photograph is required.

## Method

A representative sample of document structures is compared using fixed tokens and different composition families. The test asks whether body organisation changes in observable ways. A difference in colour alone would not answer that question. The fixtures are generated locally so network availability and image-search drift cannot decide the result.

## Limits

A structural test is not a substitute for editorial judgement. Geometry can reveal a clipped paragraph, an incorrect page field or a detached caption. It cannot prove that a photograph supports a claim or that a document feels appropriate for its audience. Those decisions need visual review and a clear brief.

## Conclusion

Conventional documents should remain conventional when that is useful. Restraint is a deliberate design choice, not a failure to add enough components. The skill must preserve this option while also supporting more expressive, asset-led documents.
